NA

Source: LEARNINGS.md

2026-05-16 (CRAN pre-test fix — 0.4.3 → 0.4.4)

  • [CPU time 4x elapsed on Debian]: r-devel-linux pre-test flagged “Running R code in ‘testthat.R’ had CPU time 4 times elapsed time” even though bibnets has zero explicit parallelism. Cause: OpenBLAS on the CRAN Debian flavor multi-threads Matrix::crossprod() / tcrossprod() inside multiply_bipartite() across all available cores. Local macOS missed it because Apple vecLib is single-threaded by default. Fix: Sys.setenv("OMP_THREAD_LIMIT" = "2") at the top of tests/testthat.R, before library(bibnets) — OpenMP caches the pool size on first use, so setting it after package load is a no-op. Use OMP_THREAD_LIMIT (hard ceiling) not OMP_NUM_THREADS (overridable default), per Writing R Extensions §1.2.1.1.
  • [Windows aspell mis-tokenises López → “pez”]: win-builder flagged pez at column 18:57 in DESCRIPTION; Debian flagged López at 18:54 in the same field. Windows aspell splits on the encoded “ó” and reports the trailing fragment. Encoding is correctly declared UTF-8 — the artifact is a Windows-only aspell quirk and only needs acknowledging in cran-comments.md, not fixing.
  • [Misspelled-words NOTE — what to acknowledge]: surnames, the canonical domain term Bibliometric/bibliometric, historiograph (real bibliometric term, Garfield 2003 doi:10.1002/asi.10307), and UK spelling normalisations. Listed in cran-comments.md with one-line justification per token.

2026-04-25 (CRAN audit session)

  • [bibnets_network class leak in to_gephi]: edge_out <- edges followed by column renames (from→Source, etc.) preserved the bibnets_network class. The S3 print.bibnets_network then looked up $from/$to/$weight and got NULL, displaying NA NA NA. The data was correct underneath; only the print output was wrong. Fix: as.data.frame(edges), class(edge_out) <- "data.frame", strip network_type/counting/similarity attributes, then rename. Lesson: when a function returns a data frame derived from a classed input and the output is semantically unrelated to the input class, explicitly strip the class.
  • [GraphML NA serialization]: sprintf('<data key="weight">%s</data>', NA_real_) produces <data key="weight">NA</data> — the literal string “NA”. Downstream parsers (Gephi, igraph::read_graph, networkx.read_graphml) interpret this as a string attribute, not a missing value. The GraphML spec way to represent missing is to omit the <data> tag entirely (the parser then uses the type’s default). Fix: data_tag() helper returns NA_character_ for NA inputs, dropped before paste() via drop_na().
  • [print.bibnets_network max() warnings]: max(nchar(x)) on an empty character vector emits no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf — even though max() returns -Inf gracefully, the warning is noisy in run_examples() output. Defensive fix: if (length(x)) max(floor, max(nchar(x))) else floor.
  • [.Rbuildignore must list every non-package top-level dir]: sidelined/ was at root with no .Rbuildignore entry → R CMD check NOTE “Non-standard file/directory found at top level”. The check is purely path-based; even if the directory has no R/ contents that the package would load, its presence triggers the NOTE. Fix: ^sidelined$.
  • [inst/WORDLIST]: aspell wordlist for devtools::spell_check() and CRAN incoming. Each line one word. Lives in inst/ (not the package root). Reduces noise so real misspellings stand out.
  • belief (“\dontrun is fine for read-* functions”) was wrong. Reviewer ruling: \dontrun{} is reserved for examples that truly cannot run (paid software, missing API keys, OS-specific tooling). For file-based readers, ship a tiny fixture in inst/extdata/ and call it via system.file() so the example runs unconditionally. For wrappers that accept upstream-package output as a data frame (e.g. read_openalex, read_crossref), construct a minimal inline data frame with the upstream column shape — that exercises the conversion path without any network call. \dontrun only stays when truly no executable form exists. Implemented across all 7 reader Rds on 2026-05-14.

2026-04-18 (equivalence-real-dataset session)

  • [build_bipartite duplicate entity entries]: Matrix::sparseMatrix(i, j, x=1) sums duplicate (i,j) pairs — if an author appears twice in one paper’s author list, B[paper, author]=2, and crossprod(B) inflates co-authorship weights multiplicatively (2×2=4 instead of 1). Fixed by deduplicating (work_idx, entity_names) pairs before sparseMatrix call. 7 papers in the OpenAlex dataset had this issue.
  • [equivalence confirmed]: bibnets full-counting co-authorship = biblionetwork full_counting (max|diff|=0). Fractional counting: max|diff|=4.4e-16 (floating point only). Bibliographic coupling + cosine: max|diff|=0. 12,270 edges all match.
  • [keyword co-occurrence needs ≥2 keywords per paper]: keyword_network returns 0 edges when each paper has exactly 1 keyword (primary_topic only from flat CSV). Cannot validate keyword co-occurrence against biblionetwork with this dataset.
  • [biblionetwork biblio_coupling default = cosine]: biblionetwork::biblio_coupling normalizes by cosine by default. bibnets equivalent: document_network(data, "coupling", counting="full", similarity="cosine").

2026-04-18 (openalex-csv session)

  • [OpenAlex flat CSV vs nested]: Flat CSV export from openalex.org uses dot-notation column names (authorships.author.display_name) and pipe (|) as multi-value separator. Distinct from openalexR::oa_fetch() output (nested list-columns). Detection fingerprint: authorships.author.display_name in header.
  • [split_field empty elements]: split_field() was not filtering empty strings after splitting — trailing/duplicate separators (e.g. “CZ||GB”) produced empty-string actor nodes. Fixed by parts[nchar(parts) > 0]. Safe change: empty actors are never valid network nodes.
  • [OpenAlex flat CSV no references]: The flat export has no references/cited_works column — only cited_by_count. Cannot build reference-based networks (coupling, co-citation) from this format.
  • [Dataset filter: NA + empty string]: filter_to_complete = no NAs AND no empty strings (trimws(x) != ""). 1,533 rows → 733 rows for the learning analytics OpenAlex dataset.

2026-04-18 (equiv-validation session)

  • [strength counting formula bug]: counting = "strength" was computing Σ IDF(r) / √(n_i × n_j) — Salton’s cosine denominator with IDF numerator — NOT the Perianes-Rodriguez (2016) formula Σ IDF(r) / (n_i × n_j). Root cause: Diagonal(sqrt(row_w)) %*% B %*% Diagonal(sqrt(idf)) symmetrically halves the row normalization, giving geometric-mean denominator. Fix: IDF applied to columns only in apply_counting; row normalization deferred to multiply_bipartite as a post-divide step via attr(B, "row_scale").
  • [biblionetwork normalizeSimilarity “cos” invalid]: bibliometrix::normalizeSimilarity(M, type="cos") fails silently (S not found). Valid type for cosine is "salton".
  • [bibliometrix coupling rownames]: biblioNetwork(bm, "coupling") returns papers labeled “1 NA 1”, “2 NA 2” (position-based). Rename rownames(M) <- bm$UT to align with bibnets paper IDs.
  • [bibliometrix co-citation node names]: Co-citation node names are truncated to “AUTHOR YEAR” format by labelShort(). Bibnets preserves the full WoS string “AUTHOR, YEAR, JOURNAL”. Align with sub("^([^,]+), *([0-9]{4}).*", "\\1 \\2", x).

2026-04-18

  • [author_weights dead code]: The fractional and paper cases in author_weights() are never called via the public API (the function is only invoked from build_author_bipartite() which is only called for positional methods). fractional = rep(1/n, n) is correct as a per-author weight and is directly tested. paper = rep(1/n, n) was wrong (comment claimed sqrt(2/(n*(n-1)))) — removed it. Correct Batagelj paper formula lives in apply_counting().
  • [normalize dual path]: normalize() has two code paths: dense (as.matrix()) for < 500 nodes, sparse triplet for >= 500. Both are correct but the dense path allocates a full matrix.
  • [two counting formulas for fractional]: apply_counting(, "fractional", "symmetric") uses Perianes-Rodriguez 1/(n-1) per shared paper. author_weights(n, "fractional") returns 1/n (simple per-author weight). These are different and both intentional — do not confuse them.

2026-04-16 (revision pass)

  • [gephi empty edge list]: $<- on a 0-row data.frame with a scalar value errors (replacement has 1 row, data has 0). Use rep(value, nrow(out)) instead.

2026-04-16 (continued)

  • [build_bipartite uppercasing]: All entity names go through toupper(trimws(...)) in build_bipartite. Tests comparing node labels must use uppercase (e.g., “ML” not “ml”, “OXFORD” not “Oxford”). This is intentional normalization.
  • [backbone alpha bounds]: backbone() validates alpha > 0 && alpha < 1 strictly. Tests cannot use alpha=1 to “keep everything” — use 0.9999 instead.
  • [expect_s3_class info arg]: testthat::expect_s3_class() does not accept an info= argument. Use expect_true(inherits(x, "cls")) when a custom failure message is needed.
  • [conetwork build_by_network]: The field entities (what nodes are) are NOT uppercased by build_by_network since it goes through a merge/aggregate path before build_bipartite. But the final build_bipartite call in that function uppercases the BY-values (the linking field), not the entity names. So in conetwork(d, "authors", by="keywords"), author names preserve their original case, but keyword values get uppercased internally.

2026-04-16

  • [output standardization]: Standard column order for all readers is: id, title, year, journal, doi, cited_by_count, abstract, type, then list-columns authors, references, keywords, then source-specific extras. Extras include index_keywords, affiliations, language (Scopus), keywords_plus (WoS), affiliations/countries (Dimensions).
  • [local_citations column order]: Output order is id, lcs, gcs (if cited_by_count present), year, title, journal, doi. Year is always coerced to integer.

2026-04-15

  • [bibliometrix cocMatrix]: Simple ref strings like “REF1” produce empty matrices. Must use WoS-style “AUTHOR YEAR JOURNAL” format for cocMatrix to parse correctly.
  • [bibliometrix normalizeSimilarity]: Uses diagonal of co-occurrence matrix as total counts. Formula implementations match the van Eck & Waltman (2009) definitions exactly.
  • [matrix multiplication counting]: For position-dependent counting (harmonic etc.), bipartite entry = positional weight. crossprod then gives link weight = w_i * w_j, which is the natural extension of positional credit to network edges.
  • [fractional vs paper counting]: fractional (1/n per entity) and paper (total per paper = 1, i.e., 2/(n*(n-1)) per link for symmetric) are different. The former normalizes per entity, the latter per paper.
  • [biblionetwork coupling]: Uses Salton’s cosine (coupling angle) by default, which equals document_network(d, "coupling", measure = "cosine") in bibnets.

2026-06-13

  • [field/sep API]: All builders + local_citations/historiograph now take field and sep. Rule chosen: sep applies ONLY to the entity field; references always splits on “;” — reference strings contain commas internally, so threading a user’s sep = "," into references would shred them.
  • [wrong-sep guard]: warn_if_sep_mismatch() warns when a split yields no multi-entry rows but ≥50% of values contain “,”, “|”, “;” or ” and “. Known false positive: an all-single-author dataset with”Last, First” names. Warning text is conditional (“If entries are separated by…”) for that reason.
  • [arg naming]: generic field rejected by user as unclear on the public surface — each builder’s column-selector arg is named after the entity (authors, keywords, references, journal, countries, affiliations). Generic field stays only on internal helpers and conetwork() (genuinely generic there). keyword_network keeps field as a deprecated warning alias because 0.4.4 shipped it on CRAN.
  • [non-breaking arg additions]: new args must go at the END of a builder’s signature, never inserted mid-list — inserting after type shifted positional binding of counting/similarity and broke fn(d, "collaboration", "fractional")-style calls. Exception: keyword_network’s column selector stays 2nd because field shipped there in 0.4.4. R CMD check needs every NEWS section title to parse as a version, so don’t leave a “(development version)” header above a numbered release.
  • [non-ASCII in R code]: literal curly quotes (U+201C/U+201D) in a regex string triggers R CMD check WARNING “Found the following file with non-ASCII characters” — comments are exempt but code is not. Use ““”/“”” escapes. tools::showNonASCIIfile() pinpoints offending lines.
  • [strip_quotes chokepoint]: implemented quote-stripping once in ensure_list_column (every builder routes columns through it) rather than at 4 separate toupper(trimws()) normalization sites. To honor strip_quotes=FALSE, the flag must also thread through build_bipartite/build_author_bipartite (they call ensure_list_column again with default TRUE otherwise). Scalar columns (source_network journal) bypass ensure_list_column and need an inline strip.
  • [references_sep design]: references kept a separate separator arg (default “;”) rather than reusing the entity sep, because reference strings contain internal commas — threading a user’s sep=“,” into references shreds them. Confirmed by code-review: author/country/institution/source coupling silently split references on “;” before this fix.
  • [sep-mismatch heuristic scope]: only warn on structural delimiters (“;”, “|”, tab) that never occur inside a single legitimate label. Commas and ” and ” are ambiguous — “Last, First” names, reference strings, and “Smith and Sons” are valid single values, so warning on them misleads users with correct data (Codex P3).
  • [strip_quotes must follow nested calls]: historiograph() splits/strips at its top, then calls local_citations() which re-runs ensure_list_column with its OWN default strip_quotes=TRUE. Must forward strip_quotes so node-selection labels match edge-building labels, else strip_quotes=FALSE gives inconsistent historiographs (Codex P2).
